name: unuran
desc: UNU.RAN - Universal Non-Uniform RANdom number generator
why: A serious random-variate generator library for arbitrary distributions, a real mathematical tool with obscure appeal.

brief.what_it_is: UNU.RAN (Universal Non-Uniform RAndom Number generator) is a C library of algorithms for generating non-uniform pseudorandom variates, meaning random numbers drawn from a chosen probability distribution rather than the uniform distribution. You supply a distribution object (the library includes standard distributions, and you can build custom, truncated, empirical or multivariate ones) and a uniform random number source, pick a method, and get a generator object that produces samples. The homepage describes it as released under the GNU GPL and written by the ARVAG project group in Vienna.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it is designed for situations where a non-standard or truncated distribution is needed, where experiments with different distribution types are made, where variates are needed for variance reduction techniques, and where fast generators of predictable quality are necessary. It was originally built for so-called black-box or universal algorithms, so you can swap distributions without rewriting the sampler.
brief.how_it_works: UNU.RAN separates distribution objects, generator objects, parameter objects, and uniform random number generators into independent pieces. You create a distribution object, choose a method, and initialize a generator; if the method does not suit the distribution, initialization fails with an error rather than silently returning wrong variates. Generators can share one uniform stream or have their own, and the homepage suggests Otmar Lendl's PRNG library as a source.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no installation steps, configuration, or first-run instructions beyond the overview. It is a C library with an object-oriented API, and the homepage points to a separate online manual and download page that I did not follow. The homepage also says a uniform PRNG is needed (Lendl's library is suggested), so you should expect to provide or link one. Note that the library is also bundled into ROOT, the R package Runuran, and SSJ.
brief.standout: Instead of offering one sampler per distribution, it treats the distribution, the method, and the generator as separate objects, and the initializer refuses methods that do not fit the distribution. It is a black-box sampling toolkit for arbitrary or empirical distributions, not just a set of normal and gamma helpers, which the homepage notes is less convenient if you only want a standard normal generator.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage carries a date of November 17, 2009 next to the author Josef Leydold, and it links to a download page, but I saw no release version, changelog, or recent commit information on the homepage itself.
brief.caveats: The homepage says the interface is more sophisticated than standard libraries, so it is not the easiest choice for a simple standard-distribution draw. The homepage's own material is dated 2009 and I could not confirm current maintenance. It is released under the GNU GPL, which affects reuse in closed-source work. The user must supply a uniform random number source, and the library exposes parameter objects that are rarely needed for usual distributions. I did not fetch the separate manual or download pages, so details there are unverified.
quotes: It is especially designed for such situations where a non-standard distribution or a truncated distribution is needed.
Originally designed as a library for so called black-box or universal algorithms its interface is different from other libraries.

If the choosen method is not suitable for the given distribution (or if the distribution object contains too little information about the distribution) the initialization routine fails and produces an error message.
